profile.campus: Stream PHXA campus, Goodyear, AZ (planned 7 buildings, 157 acres, 280 MW at full build)
profile.reading: Stream Data Centers PHX-1 sits at 2950 South Litchfield Road in Goodyear, Arizona, part of Stream large PHXA campus. Per Stream own site, the full campus is planned as seven buildings across 157 acres, targeting 280 megawatts and more than 2 million square feet at full build-out, with an on-site Arizona Public Service substation ultimately capable of 480 megawatts. As of Stream own current site content, the first two buildings on the campus were actively serving tenants while the remaining five were still in development, but Stream site does not publish a dedicated page or building-specific capacity and square footage figures for PHX-1 as distinct from the overall campus totals, so no individual capacity or square footage figure is assigned to this record, only the campus-level context. No tenant is named for PHX-1 specifically. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners, a larger commercial real estate firm. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds announced acquisition of a majority stake in Stream in August 2025 and completed the deal in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. The company markets its wholesale, powered-shell, and build-to-suit data center model, claiming more than 90 percent of its capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers and describing a pipeline exceeding four gigawatts with more than 27 delivered developments across its US markets. Goodyear sits in the West Valley submarket of metro Phoenix, an area that has become one of the fastest-growing hyperscale data center corridors in the United States over the past several years, driven by available land, a favorable regulatory environment, and substantial Arizona Public Service grid investment, all factors consistent with Stream decision to plan a campus of this scale in that specific location.
profile.research_note: Campus-level 280 MW / 157 acre / 7-building PHXA figures sourced to Stream own Phoenix location page, explicitly not assigned to this individual PHX-1 building since no per-building figures are published. Company background from Stream own history/news pages.

reading.body:
Stream Data Centers' Goodyear, Arizona facility exists but its power capacity remains unknown, reflecting how sparse public information is on operational data centers even after ownership changes.

Stream Data Centers was acquired by Apollo Global Management in November 2025, with the majority stake going to Apollo while the operator retained minority ownership and continued management. The company operates more than twenty campuses across major U.S. markets with a development pipeline exceeding four gigawatts and reports over ninety percent capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers. The Goodyear location occupies 157 acres with seven buildings planned, though only two were complete at last company disclosure.

The absence of power data for this facility limits what can be known about its contribution to AI infrastructure in Arizona. The mismatch between operational and transparent capacity metrics across the industry means neither investors nor policymakers have reliable visibility into how much computing power particular regions actually hold or are building.
